name: South Korea
governanceModel: First comprehensive cross-sector AI law, paired with a state-backed sovereign model push
debateTopics: AI Basic Act enforcement decree's narrow high-risk definition
Sovereign foundation-model push vs. matching frontier performance
overview:
South Korea's AI Basic Act took effect on 22 January 2026 — the world's first comprehensive, cross-sector AI legal framework — with the Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) enforcing a roughly one-year grace period on fines and investigations (with exceptions for serious harm) while substantive compliance duties apply immediately.

Alongside binding regulation, MSIT selected five teams — Naver Cloud, Upstage, SK Telecom, NC AI and LG AI Research — to build homegrown sovereign foundation models with state-subsidised compute, targeting at least 95% of frontier-model performance, reassessed every six months through 2027. Civil society groups and human-rights lawyers have criticised the Act's enforcement decree for defining 'high-risk AI' too narrowly, offering weak protection against AI impersonation and fraud.

debates.topic: AI Basic Act enforcement decree's narrow high-risk definition
debates.summary: Civil-society groups argue the Act's implementing decree defines 'high-risk AI' too narrowly, leaving weak protection against AI impersonation and fraud.
debates.expanded: Human-rights lawyers and civil-society groups say the enforcement decree's scope — relying mainly on watermarking requirements and fines — is too limited given the scale of AI-enabled fraud and impersonation risks. Industry counters that a stricter definition would undercut Korea's competitiveness just as it's trying to build sovereign frontier capability.

debates.topic: Sovereign foundation-model push vs. matching frontier performance
debates.summary: Korea's five state-backed teams are being held to a concrete, reassessed target of matching 95%+ of frontier-model performance — a high bar with a hard review cycle.
debates.expanded: Unlike open-ended national AI investment elsewhere, Korea's programme has a specific, numeric performance target reassessed every six months through 2027 — creating real pressure on Naver, Upstage, SK Telecom, NC AI and LG AI Research to show measurable progress against US and Chinese frontier labs rather than simply receiving indefinite state support.
